content: These references include studies, guidelines, reports, and reviews from organizations such as the World Health Organization (WHO), UNAIDS, and various academic journals. 1. The third edition of the International Standards for Tuberculosis Care was published in The Hague by TB CARE 1. This document outlines global standards for the management and care of tuberculosis patients. It was accessed on October 8, 2015. 2. The International Guidelines on HIV/AIDS and Human Rights: Consolidated Version was published in Geneva by the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) and UNAIDS. This document provides a framework for addressing human rights in the context of HIV/AIDS. It was accessed on October 5, 2015. 3. The Patients’ Charter for Tuberculosis Care was developed by the World Care Council in the USA. This charter defines the rights and responsibilities of tuberculosis patients. It was accessed on October 8, 2015. 4. A report titled Assessment of Compulsory Treatment of People Who Use Drugs in Cambodia, China, Malaysia, and Viet Nam was published by the WHO Western Pacific Region. This document evaluates the application of human rights principles in drug treatment programs. It was accessed on October 8, 2015. 5. The United Nations issued a Joint Statement on Compulsory Drug Detention and Rehabilitation Centres in Geneva. This statement addresses the human rights concerns associated with such facilities. It was accessed on October 8, 2015. 6. The WHO published a technical paper titled Effectiveness of Interventions to Address HIV in Prisons, which reviews evidence-based strategies for managing HIV in correctional settings. It was accessed on October 8, 2015. 7. The International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (Resolution 2200A [XXI]) was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly in New York. This foundational human rights treaty was accessed on October 8, 2015. 8. Harris and Rhodes conducted a review on Hepatitis C Treatment Access and Uptake for People Who Inject Drugs, highlighting the role of social factors in treatment outcomes. This study was published in the journal Harm Reduction Journal in 2013. 9. Kerschberger et al. investigated the impact of integrating HIV and TB services on the time to initiation of antiretroviral therapy (ART) in a before-and-after study. Their findings were published in PLOS One in 2012. 10. A rapid assessment of the accessibility and integration of HIV, TB, and harm reduction services for people who inject drugs in Portugal was conducted by the WHO Regional Office for Europe. This report was accessed on October 8, 2015. 11. The WHO published a handbook titled Tuberculosis Prevalence Surveys, which provides guidance on conducting TB prevalence studies. It was accessed on October 8, 2015. 12. Hyle et al. reviewed the costs, effects, and cost-effectiveness of integrated care for HIV, TB, and non-communicable diseases. Their findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2014. 13. Atun et al. used a system dynamics simulation model to evaluate the impact of integrated HIV harm reduction and multidrug-resistant TB control programs in Estonia. This study was published in Health Policy in 2007. 14. The WHO published the ENGAGE-TB Implementation Manual, which provides guidance on integrating community-based TB activities into the work of non-governmental and civil society organizations. It was accessed on January 27, 2016. 15. Sculier, Getahun, and Lienhardt emphasized the importance of operational research in improving TB prevention, diagnosis, and treatment among people living with HIV. Their work was published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2011. 16. The WHO identified priority research questions for TB/HIV in resource-limited settings in a report titled Priority Research Questions for TB/HIV. This document was accessed on October 8, 2015. 17. Ethical considerations in biomedical HIV prevention trials were addressed in a joint publication by UNAIDS and WHO. This document was accessed on October 5, 2015. 18. The WHO published a guide for monitoring and evaluating collaborative TB/HIV activities, revised in 2015. This guide was accessed on October 5, 2015. 19. Bachireddy et al. demonstrated that integrating health services improved multiple healthcare outcomes among HIV-infected people who inject drugs in Ukraine. Their study was published in Drug and Alcohol Dependence in 2014. 20. Wolfe, Carrieri, and Shepard reviewed barriers to treatment and care for injecting drug users with HIV infection and proposed strategies to overcome these challenges. Their findings were published in The Lancet in 2010. 21. Malotte et al. compared the effectiveness of incentives versus outreach workers in promoting latent TB treatment among drug users. Their study was published in the American Journal of Preventive Medicine in 2001. 22. Des Jarlais et al. evaluated the provision of hepatitis B vaccination to injection drug users through referral to health clinics versus on-site vaccination at syringe exchange programs. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Public Health in 2001. 23. Gourevitch et al. reported on the successful adherence to observed prophylaxis and treatment of TB among drug users in a methadone program. This study was published in the Journal of Addictive Diseases in 1996. 24. Smirnoff et al. described the implementation of directly observed therapy (DOT) for TB in an inner-city hospital. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 1998. 25. Dhingra et al. shared the experience of implementing DOTS for drug addicts with TB in Delhi, India. Their study was published in the Indian Journal of Tuberculosis in 2008. 26. Rüütel et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial to enhance TB case detection among substitution treatment patients. Their findings were published in BMC Research Notes in 2011. 27. Snyder et al. evaluated the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of TB prevention in methadone maintenance clinics. Their study was published in the American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine in 1999. 28. Rich et al. highlighted the successful linkage of medical care and community services for HIV-positive offenders being released from prison. Their study was published in the Journal of Urban Health in 2001. 29. Morozova et al. demonstrated that methadone treatment improved TB treatment outcomes among hospitalized opioid-dependent patients in Ukraine. Their study was published in the International Journal of Drug Policy in 2013. 30. The WHO published the Global Update on HIV Treatment 2013, summarizing results, impacts, and opportunities in HIV care. This report was accessed on October 8, 2015.
